title: Usage Preference Atlas & Competitive Friction Scorecard for Model Selection
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Produce a normalized Usage Preference Atlas that maps enterprise buyer preferences (latency, cost, hallucination risk, quantization tolerance) across top open and commercial models, and deliver a Competitive Friction Scorecard that quantifies switching cost and operational risk for each model-family.
description:
Problem: Sales and Solutions teams keep asking: for our enterprise RAG customers which models are easiest to switch to (low friction) vs high friction due to latency/cost/compatibility? We need a repeatable, data-driven artifact to prioritize model sourcing and fallback orchestration.

Scope:
- Inventory top 12 candidate models (open + major commercial) used by customers and prospects.
- Collect signals: token cost, median p95 latency (50/256 tokens), quantized accuracy delta, embedding drift sensitivity, licensing constraints, hardware affinity, and telemetry-derived error/failure modes.
- Normalize signals into a Usage Preference Atlas (spreadsheet + canonical schema) that allows filtering by vertical (finance, health, SMB) and workload (RAG, chat, embeddings).
- Build a Competitive Friction Scorecard: composite score (0-100) representing effort to adopt/replace a model in production taking into account operational changes, retraining/finetuning needs, and compliance/legal gating.

Deliverables:
1) Usage Preference Atlas (Google Sheet) with data provenance and raw sources.
2) Scoring rubric document and reproducible scoring notebook (Python).
3) 10-slide GTM-friendly deck summarizing top risk buckets and recommended fallback pairings.
4) PRD stub for integrating Atlas into Model Watchtower feeds.

Stakeholders: Solutions (Rajiv), Sales Engineering (Marta), Runtime (Sofia), Research (Eve).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical atlas sheet populated for 12 models with provenance columns and normalization method
Friction Scorecard rubric documented and validated with at least 2 Solutions use-cases
Demo deck reviewed by Sales Eng and Research with sign-off from PM (Aisha)
Prototype scoring notebook pushed to repo and linked in PRD (model-watchtower)
decisions: Primary cost axis will be normalized token-cost (USD/token) using region-adjusted pricing; compute-only inference credits will be converted using our internal cost model
Latency importance weight will be 1.5x for RAG workloads versus chat-only workloads in the composite score
Open-model license incompatibilities will be flagged as hard friction (score penalty 35) rather than probabilistic risk
Initial model list restricted to 12 to keep manual validation tractable; will expand after automation pipeline is proven
